title: REL05-BP06 Make services stateless where possible
book_use: Technical precedent for externalizing state so replaceable compute resources can service requests and individual-node failure is easier to tolerate.; Chapters: 2;3;5;23; Caveat: Cloud application guidance rather than agent research; used as an architectural analogy.

title: Event Sourcing
book_use: Defines event sourcing as capturing state changes as a sequence of events and discusses reconstruction temporal queries replay and parallel timelines.; Chapters: 3;7;11;13;14; Caveat: Influential practitioner writing from 2005; event sourcing has real complexity and is not prescribed for every agent.

title: What do you mean by Event-Driven?
book_use: Distinguishes event notification event-carried state transfer event sourcing and CQRS; supports precision about event-driven agent architecture.; Chapters: 3;5;7;15; Caveat: Conceptual taxonomy rather than empirical evaluation.

title: Temporal Platform Documentation
book_use: Contemporary example of durable execution where workflow state survives crashes outages timers and worker replacement through persisted history and replay.; Chapters: 5;7;12;23;24; Caveat: Vendor documentation; demonstrates an available architecture but not independent evidence of agent correctness.

title: Durable Execution Solutions
book_use: States that workflow state can be recovered replayed or paused across failures and provides task queues timers retries and persisted application state.; Chapters: 5;12;18;23;24; Caveat: Vendor marketing language; use for architectural existence rather than performance claims.

title: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
book_use: Explains why retryable distributed operations need idempotent contracts to avoid repeated side effects after ambiguous failure.; Chapters: 5;20;23; Caveat: General distributed-systems guidance rather than AI-specific evidence.

title: REL04-BP04 Make mutating operations idempotent
book_use: Provides reliability guidance for repeated mutating requests and idempotency tokens in distributed systems.; Chapters: 5;20;23; Caveat: General cloud architecture guidance; exact semantics vary by system.

title: Anthropic Economic Index report: Cadences
book_use: Product telemetry and surveys showing Anthropic usage shifting from conversation toward longer-running agentic tasks and more automated work sessions.; Chapters: 1;5;9;12;18;24; Caveat: Vendor/product-specific evidence and self-report; not representative of all workers or agent systems.
